design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Marcy asks only 'how much do I pay to get PrePay started, and let me pay it'. The scored root is the activation payment (102.19): an opening target (cover days x opening daily cost) less the prepaid balance standing on the enrollment. The activation rule says the payment is quoted only after the prepaid balance carries the carried-in credit for a credit balance that stood on the enrolled service account when the enrollment was taken. Service account 3aad4393-52c1-4fcf-a797-d6e2833de703 stands at -232.59 (a LIHEAP payment of 450.00 on 2026-09-25 and her own mailed check of 60.00 on 2026-09-29 overpaid the August and September bills) and the enrollment ledger is empty, so the agent must first compute and book the carried-in credit under the carry-in rule (credit balance less a cut-over reserve for the usage not yet billed, less a hold on an uncleared check) = 30.59, and only then quote the activation payment on the balance that credit produced. Both computations reconcile 13 standard bills, payments, a returned e-check, late charges, a reconnect fee, a medical certificate and two other products (capital credit allocations, an arrangement ledger). Each rule names its own target tool in the charter (target_tool); the published rule text names no tool.

SCOPE (task 0 of 2). Claimed: prepay_ext_postpaid_credit_carry_in (owner=agent tool post_carried_credit_69e6c97d, subject prepay_credit_adjustment with reason postpaid_credit_transfer) and prepay_ext_activation_payment (owner=user tool make_activation_payment_0416a855, subject prepay_payment on an enrollment awaiting activation). Task 1 claims the meter error refund (prepay_credit_adjustment with reason meter_error_refund, its own tool), the alert reset and the restore payment. Disjoint.

DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [5, 5]. Carry-in: 5 factors (1 method, 4 parameter); activation: 5 factors (1 method, 4 parameter). Multi-source over the task: uncleared_payment_hold (every non-fall-through tier combines the latest payment's channel and date with the returned-payment count over a different record) and payment_habit_cover_days (latest channel AND a 3-month channel count). Cross-difficulty: patronage_reserve_days (capital ledger) and arrangement_history_cover_days (arrange ledger), the others reading service records.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root prepay_ext_activation_payment. Edge root -> prepay_ext_postpaid_credit_carry_in: value_input, gate balance_on_enrollment, form state, policy_source 'The activation payment is quoted only after the prepaid balance of the enrollment carries the carried-in credit for a credit balance that stood on the enrolled service account when the enrollment was taken.'. Four-point test: 'only after' joins this policy's result (the quoted activation payment) to a record-visible state (a carried-in credit entry on the enrollment ledger, sourced on the service account, included in the prepaid balance); no tool, id or code token; closed scope 'a credit balance that stood on the enrolled service account when the enrollment was taken'. Exactly one write of the difficulty books a carried-in standard-billing credit: the carry-in rule's target tool (the meter refund tool writes the meter error reason, the others write payments or an alert amount). Unresolved at frozen_time: initial_state.service_accounts.3aad4393-52c1-4fcf-a797-d6e2833de703.account_balance = -232.59 and no prepay_ledger row exists; initial_state.prepay_accounts.d374a83d-76e9-4e82-b68d-8365b87a44c2.prepaid_balance = 0.0. Flips: a postpaid_credit_transfer entry of 30.59 with source 3aad4393-52c1-4fcf-a797-d6e2833de703 and prepaid_balance 30.59. Order: carry-in (call step 11) then activation (call step 16). Deletion sensitivity: skipping the carry-in gives activation 132.78 instead of 102.19. user_scenario never asks for the credit; her only related line is a passive reaction if the agent mentions money left over. Tools validate nothing.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. prepay_credit_adjustment is governed by prepay_evt_enrollment_transfers (no eligibility; policy_scope). Two base sentences are superseded and declared in overwrite: prepay_agg_member_arrears 'A credit balance on the enrolled service account is carried in ... and is never netted against another account's debt.' (replaced by the carried-in credit sentence; 'never netted' is restated in the scope sentence) and prepay_evt_enrollment_transfers' credit-adjustment sentence ('for the difference only and once per source record', replaced by the scope sentence, which keeps 'booked once'). No sibling charter fixes the carried amount (service: a final credit is refunded only on a final bill; the service account here is active). Tier check: arrears measure = positive balance of the enrolled account 0.00 + no final-billed account = 0.00 -> PrePay Power Residential, matching the enrollment. No security deposit is held on the account, so no deposit release is owed (the deposit charter's release does not arise). prepay_payment: prepay_evt_activation (gates apply to prepay_activate only -> policy_scope) and prepay_evt_payment_split payment_limits (102.19 within 10.00-500.00; phone_ivr_card allowed). The activation window (14 days from 2026-10-01, inclusive) is open; it governs the later system activation.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Carried-in credit: object = the credit balance of service account 3aad4393-52c1-4fcf-a797-d6e2833de703 (correlation: source_reference_id = the service account). Kept back: the cut-over reserve (usage from the 2026-09-12 bill to 2026-10-01) and the hold on the 2026-09-29 mailed check 518d22f4-0dcb-48b5-86d1-9cf5baade28b (60.00, could still be returned; the member had e-check 2b7343a4-846b-46eb-8df2-419f6d70d20f returned 2026-03-20). The LIHEAP agency payment is not a check and is not held. Activation: object = enrollment d374a83d-76e9-4e82-b68d-8365b87a44c2; the payment row carries prepay_account_id.

FACTOR CARD - carried-in credit (baseline: credit 232.59 less 19 days x last bill 170.12/30, hold 0; baseline_result 124.85). reserve_daily_cost_basis (method): 12 bills in the window and last bill 1120 kWh x 12 < 16190 -> 2355.99/365 = 6.4548/day; baseline 47.84. uncleared_payment_hold (parameter, multi-source): latest payment 2026-09-29 mail_check 60.00 in the one-month window AND one return in 12 months -> hold 60.00 (near-miss: the later-dated-looking LIHEAP 450.00 of 2026-09-25 is an agency payment and earlier); baseline 90.59. late_charge_reserve_days (parameter): late charges 2026-04-02 and 2026-09-02 (2) -> +3; baseline 49.95. reconnect_reserve_days (parameter): remote reconnect fee 2025-06-18 inside 24 months -> +3; baseline 49.95. patronage_reserve_days (parameter, capital): 17 distribution-margin allocations (near-miss: 10 gt rows) -> -3; baseline 11.22. Reserve days 19+3+3-3 = 22; reserve 142.00; credit 232.59 - 142.00 - 60.00 = 30.59.

FACTOR CARD - activation payment (baseline 7 days x last bill/30 - balance, floor 50.00; baseline_result 50.0). payment_habit_cover_days (parameter, multi-source): latest payment mail_check 2026-09-29 and 3 mailed checks in 3 months -> 14; baseline 57.93. opening_daily_cost_basis (method): larger of last bill 170.12 and the 2025-09 bill 189.69, /30 = 6.323; baseline 88.49. medical_certificate_cover_days: certificate 2025-12-08 -> +4; baseline 76.9. arrangement_history_cover_days (arrange): missed installment 2025-05-22, no default -> +2; baseline 89.55. late_charge_cover_days: 2 late charges -> +1; baseline 95.87. 21 days x 6.323 = 132.78; payment 132.78 - 30.59 = 102.19.

SEED ROWS AND WHY. customers, service_accounts (active, balance -232.59 equal to the 13-month history from zero, the 2025-06 reconnect fee settled before it), 39 usage lines, 2 late charges, 1 returned-payment fee, 1 reconnect fee, 15 payments (incl. the LIHEAP agency payment and the mailed check), 1 return, the LIHEAP pledge it fulfilled, 1 expired medical certificate, capital account + 17 DM + 10 gt allocations + 1 retirement, arrangement + ledger, prepay enrollment (pending_activation, prepaid 0.00) and the signed agreement. Revision 2 (audit F-1/F-2): the security deposit record and its interest bill credit were removed and the prerequisite was changed from a deposit release to the carried-in credit, because the deposit charter fixes the release amount and no prepay overwrite can change it.

PERSONA. Opens with the surface goal, gives membership number and phone only when asked, authorises postings passively, reacts to a mention of left-over money with 'I may have paid September twice' only after the agent raises it, accepts the amount, pays in person on the phone payment line, declines alert changes, closes after the payment confirms.

STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers -> verify -> service account -> enrollment -> agreement -> enrollment ledger (no credit) -> service charges -> service payments -> capital account and ledger -> carried-in credit 30.59 (agent) -> certificates -> arrangements -> arrange ledger -> the member pays 102.19 (user).

POLICY/GT CLOSURE. carry-in -> post_carried_credit_69e6c97d -> computations[0] step 11 carried_amount 30.59; activation -> make_activation_payment_0416a855 -> computations[1] step 16 gross_payment_amount 102.19; terminal prepaid_balance 132.78. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies in order. Draft from the visible charters: no sibling charter states a different carried amount, so one answer pair.

AUDIT ROUND 2 CLOSURE. F-1 closed by removing the deposit-release problem (no deposit in this world, new carry-in prerequisite); F-2 closed with it (the carry-in reads only the enrolled account, as the base credit-balance sentence does, and that sentence is declared in overwrite); multi-source claim corrected (uncleared_payment_hold and payment_habit_cover_days carry it; reserve_daily_cost_basis is not claimed). Per-task and final gates re-run after the rework: see task 1's closing section.
user_scenario: You are Marcy Gentry, fifty-eight, a school cafeteria cook in Harlan Springs who has had her electricity from Cedar Fork at the same house on Possum Trot Road since 2009. Money has been tight since spring, and on October 1 you went into the district office and signed up to switch the house over to PrePay Power; you signed the PrePay paperwork right there at the counter. The woman at the office told you the meter switches over to prepay once your first payment is made. You are calling this morning to find out how much that first payment has to be, and you want to pay it today with your debit card. You open with something like: "Hi, this is Marcy Gentry. I signed up for that PrePay last week and I need to know what I have to pay to get it started. I'd like to go ahead and pay it today." Only when the representative asks you to verify who you are do you give your membership number, 0421376, and your phone number, 2705552418; you do not remember the date you joined, and you would rather not read out your Social Security digits unless they still cannot find you. You know no account number by heart besides the membership number. You have no idea how the cooperative figures the payment and you do not try to guess; you just want the number and want the whole thing settled on this call. If the representative tells you they first have to post or move something on your account, you tell them to go ahead. If they mention money left over on your regular electric account, you say you think you may have paid your September bill twice: you mailed a check before you knew the LIHEAP help had come through, and you leave it there. When they give you the amount you accept it as it is, without haggling. If they ask how you want to pay, you say your debit card, over the phone. You pay it yourself: when the representative hands you the phone payment line, you put in exactly the amount they told you, and once it goes through you read back the confirmation number if they ask for it. If they ask whether you want your low-balance text alerts changed, you say no, the texts are fine the way the office set them up. Once the payment has gone through and they have confirmed it, you thank them and end the call.

edges.condition: The enrollment's PrePay ledger carries a credit-adjustment entry with the reason carried-in standard-billing credit whose source is the enrolled service account, and the prepaid balance includes it.
edges.policy_source: The activation payment is quoted only after the prepaid balance of the enrollment carries the carried-in credit for a credit balance that stood on the enrolled service account when the enrollment was taken.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The enrolled service account stands at a credit balance and the enrollment's ledger carries no carried-in credit entry, so the prepaid balance does not carry it.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 11 creates a prepay_credit_adjustment postpaid_credit_transfer entry with source 3aad4393-52c1-4fcf-a797-d6e2833de703 and sets prepaid_balance to 30.59.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, no parallel prerequisites: the carried-in credit must land first because the activation payment reads the prepaid balance it changes.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the carried-in credit leaves prepaid_balance 0.00, the activation payment becomes 132.78 instead of 102.19, and the credit entry is missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only what to pay to start PrePay and to pay it; it never asks for a credit or mentions one first; her line about possibly paying September twice fires only after the agent mentions money left over.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: make_activation_payment_0416a855 creates the payment row and raises prepaid_balance whatever the ledger holds; post_carried_credit_69e6c97d creates the credit row and raises prepaid_balance; neither reads the service account, the ledger or any status, and neither returns an error.
